messages:
maria: Heads-up: ran a 1h replay vs synthetic for the kernel-switch patch. p95 mostly stable, but p99 jumps ~2.2x on some kernels. KV cache misses spike during tails — attaching notes and a small flame snippet.

tyler: Can you paste the loadgen config you used? Did you keep the same query distribution between replay and synthetic?

maria: ```
loadgen:
  mode: replay
  rate: 400 qps
  concurrency: auto
  microbatch_size: 16
  kv_warmup: false
  jitter_ms: 0
```

aj: Quick question: did you try pinning a kernel (no dynamic switch) to see if switching jitter causes the tail?

maria: Pinned -> p99 spikes reduce in some cases, but median increases ~7%. So it's a tradeoff: pinning helps tail but hurts steady latency.

sam: What about microbatch sizing? 8 vs 16 vs 32? That often moves p95/p99 in opposite directions.

maria: Ran 8/16/32: 8 -> p99 down but throughput -18%. 16 -> baseline. 32 -> throughput up but p99 worse and convoys appear.

leo: @tyler I think the dominant culprit for the p99 is KV eviction behavior, not kernel arithmetic. Flame snippet shows `kv_eviction` hotspots lined up with tail events.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: test/benchmark/2009000001 completed. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/test/2009000001/artifacts (flamegraphs + logs)

aj: Also important: how we measure p99. Use HdrHistogram per-request sampling with 1ms resolution (not aggregated per-token). Per-token aggregation hides request-level convoys.

maria: I reprocessed traces with hdr + per-request buckets. p99 then matches what production traces show (user complaints).

tyler: Replays tend to be too smooth — add small interarrival jitter to mimic client behavior. Try jitter_ms: 5-50 to surface convoys.

maria: ```
loadgen:
  mode: replay
  rate: 400 qps
  microbatch_size: 16
  jitter_ms: 5-50
  kv_warmup: false
```

maria: Adding 5-50ms jitter reduced convoy incidence for the kernel-switch case and improved p99 ~15%, but cold KV misses still dominate the worst tails.

sam: Proposal: allow dynamic kernel switching but implement a fast-path for cached KV hits that uses the low-latency kernel; fall back to slower kernel for misses. That keeps median low and contains miss tails.

leo: And surface per-route p95/p99 in Console so product teams can see which prompts cause worst tails. The routing layer could pick different microbatch sizes per route too.

maria: Action items: 1) @aj run 3x pinned vs dynamic + jittered replay + hdr per-request; 2) @tyler prototype KV-prefetch for top-5 prefixes; 3) infra add per-route tail dashboards (per-request histograms). I'll upload logs & config to the artifact link.

aj: :thumbsup: kicking off runs now, will post links when done.

tyler: If KV-prefetch cuts cold-hit latency we can lower conservative microbatch sizing and reclaim throughput headroom.

maria: TL;DR: kernel pinning helps p99 but raises median; jittered replay reduces synthetic-smoothing of convoys; KV miss hotspots are the major p99 driver — need combined approach (prefetch/caching + per-route SLOs + measurement hygiene). Filing follow-up in #eng-runtime with artifact links.
